Investigation: Structure and Liftoff in Combustion Experiment (SLICE)
Hardware: Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG) / SPICE flow-duct hardware
Material: Methane, ethylene and nitrogen-diluted mixtures of these gaseous fuels
Key_Finding: NASA SLICE investigated the structure and liftoff stability of gaseous laminar diffusion flames in microgravity aboard the ISS. Methane, ethylene and nitrogen-diluted fuel mixtures were studied. Flame structure and liftoff velocity limits were examined as functions of fuel and burner diameter. Flame temperature, soot and CH* radical concentrations were measured and compared with computational results. The cleared scalar fields are not represented by one universal experimental condition.
Earth_Application: Potential Earth relevance: improved understanding of flame structure and liftoff may support practical combustion-device design, fuel-efficiency research and pollutant-emission reduction. These are potential research benefits, not demonstrated Moon-base atmosphere results.
